summary: This is a Docusaurus plugin that creates individual page routes for each blog tag instead of using a single dynamic route. By enumerating all actual tags at build time, it allows Docusaurus's link checker to verify that tag links like `/blog/tags/docker` are real routes, preventing false positives when checking for broken links across the site.

explanations.20: This imports a helper function from another file that reads the blog's file structure and returns all the unique tag slugs (URL-friendly tag names).
explanations.22: In Docusaurus, a plugin is exported as a function that receives the site's configuration context and returns an object describing what the plugin does.
explanations.28: This method tells Docusaurus which files to watch for changes; if any blog posts are added or modified, the plugin will re-run and pick up new tags without restarting the dev server.
explanations.29: This glob pattern matches all index.md and index.mdx files nested anywhere inside the blog folder — these are the blog post files that contain tag metadata.
explanations.31: The `contentLoaded` method runs after Docusaurus processes all the content; the `actions` object provides methods to programmatically add routes to the site.
explanations.32: This loop runs once for each unique tag slug found in the blog posts.
explanations.33: For each tag, we tell Docusaurus to create a new route at a specific path.
